insights.title: On Building at the AI Frontier
insights.body: The engineers who will matter in 5 years aren't the ones who learned to use AI tools. They're the ones who understand why those tools work — and build on top of that understanding. Glass Box started because I kept seeing people use LLMs like black boxes. The moment you understand tokenization, attention, and decoding, you write better prompts.

insights.title: On Frontend Architecture
insights.body: Most frontend bugs aren't UI bugs. They're state management failures — race conditions, uncoordinated data fetching, cascading invalidations. The React Query orchestrator pattern I've been refining solves this at the root: sequential bootstrap with chained enabled gates. One source of truth. No chaos.

insights.title: On Personal Branding for Engineers
insights.body: Engineers underinvest in signal. You have the receipts — the PRs, the architecture decisions, the bugs nobody else wanted to touch. Share the thinking, not the jargon. LinkedIn posts that explain AI concepts to non-technical founders outperform anything written for peer engineers. Warm and human beats corporate and polished. Every time.

insights.title: On the jangya. Name
insights.body: It's Sanskrit/Odia. It means knowledge, wisdom, awareness. Pronounced like jug-ya. Most people get it wrong on the first try. The second try always lands. The name carries more than any bio ever could.
